title: Sequential hot-wall creep assessment release contract
purpose: Verify the reduced heat-transfer, thermoelastic-stress, governing-stress extraction, Kachanov--Rabotnov material-point assessment, and result-history path used by the first-release power-component demonstration.
physics: sequential transient heat conduction, plane-strain thermoelasticity, and local creep-damage assessment

execution.evidence: Four heat increments, one thermoelastic solve, and forty exact K-R material-point updates must complete and produce the versioned governing stress, rupture estimate, and end damage.

observables: Maximum sampled thermoelastic von Mises stress driving the local assessment.
K-R rupture-time estimate for the declared illustrative parameters.
Damage at ninety percent of the analytical rupture time.
Material-point strain, damage, and modified-theta histories plus FEM field artifacts.
acceptance: Heat and thermoelastic component results pass the engineering quality policy.
Every versioned observable satisfies its Golden tolerance.
The release result passes the release quality policy and materializes all declared artifacts.
The manifest states that K-R damage is a governing-point assessment rather than the separate global isothermal power-law creep field solve.

quantities.name: governing_von_mises_stress
quantities.description: Maximum quadrature-sampled plane-strain thermoelastic von Mises stress on the reduced release mesh.

quantities.name: predicted_rupture_time
quantities.description: Analytical K-R rupture-time estimate under the versioned governing stress and illustrative parameters.

quantities.name: assessment_end_damage
quantities.description: Damage after forty material-point updates ending at ninety percent of the analytical rupture time.

limitations: This is a versioned implementation regression, not material calibration or experimental validation.
Creep and damage are evaluated at one governing sampled stress; no global stress redistribution is solved.
The parameters are illustrative and must not be used for component-life decisions.
